title: Verify pre-commit account deletion failure preserves account files
classification: No new implementation defect reproduced. A synthetic deletion transaction failure rolls back the account and cleanup queue before any owned file is purged.

scenario.records: An admin and member with an uploaded avatar and thumbnail in a synthetic managed storage root.
scenario.injection: Fail the deletion transaction commit once after relation changes and file cleanup jobs have been staged.
scenario.expected: The member row remains, both files remain byte-for-byte intact, and no purge job survives the rollback.

verification.result: passed: 8 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.database: Fresh uniquely named PostgreSQL test database upgraded through d6e7f8a9b0c1.
verification.cleanup: The disposable database was dropped after the passing run.
verification.other_cases: The same run covers retained household chat and custom emoji, private relation cleanup, survivor credential isolation, failed post-commit unlink retry, unsafe-path rejection, the deletion manifest, and FK inventory.

limits: The synthetic failure exercises the database commit boundary; it does not emulate process termination at every instruction.
Operator-schema comparison, deployment restart/retry, and the P2-09 relation tabletop remain open.
